records.title: Health Care Language for Health Informatics and Information Management
records.header: HIHIM 400 Health Care Language for Health Informatics and Information Management (3)
records.departmentName: Health Informatics and Health Information Management (HIHIM)
records.text: HIHIM 400 Health Care Language for Health Informatics and Information Management (3) Students compile a working vocabulary in health care and learn to explain clinical documentation. Strengthens student competence to read, write, comprehend, and speak the language used by health providers and administrators. Employs a variety of tools (reading, writing, and listening exercises; electronic health record documents and case studies; mini-lectures on body systems). Practices written and verbal communication to achieve proficiency. Prerequisite: BIOL 118 and BIOL 119. Offered: A.

records.title: Research Design and Statistics for HIHIM
records.header: HIHIM 425 Research Design and Statistics for HIHIM (3)
records.departmentName: Health Informatics and Health Information Management (HIHIM)
records.text: HIHIM 425 Research Design and Statistics for HIHIM (3) Explores healthcare and research statistics. Addresses hospital statistics, used to calculate usage levels of heathcare resources and outcomes of clinical operations, and research statistics, used to summarize and describe significant characteristics of a data set, and to make inferences about a population based on data collected from a sample. In addition, principles of research are described, including the Institutional Review Board process. Offered: jointly with BIOST 406/STAT 406.

records.departmentName: Health Informatics and Health Information Management (HIHIM)
records.text: HIHIM 456 Quality Improvement in Healthcare (5) Focuses on quality improvement, risk management, and utilization management in healthcare; design and management of quality improvement systems, including the use of data systems in quality improvement and visual daily management systems; health data retrieval, analysis, and presentation. Prerequisite: HIHIM 400 and HIHIM 410; recommended: descriptive statistics; probability; random sampling; simple linear regression; correlation; and tests of hypotheses (either BIOST 310, EDPSY 490, QMETH 201, STAT 220, or equivalent).
